final_candidates.decision_summary: Corresponds to Q498R, introducing favorable electrostatic contacts and salt bridges with human ACE2 D38 while scoring exceptionally high in PLM plausibility.
Corresponds to N501Y, forming critical aromatic stacking and hydrogen bonds with ACE2 residues Y41 and K353, driving substantial affinity gains.
Corresponds to Y453F, which optimizes hydrophobic packing against ACE2 H34 with maximal sequence PLM score and well-documented enhanced ACE2 binding.

stop_reason.detail: Sufficient biological and computational evidence gathered to finalize the Top-3 ACE2 affinity-enhancing candidates.

history.rationale: Equivalent to N501Y, forming optimal aromatic and cation-pi packing with ACE2 residues Y41 and K353 to markedly increase receptor affinity.
ESM-1v score of 0.699 confirms evolutionary plausibility, while deep mutational scanning benchmarks identify N171Y (N501Y) as the premier ACE2 affinity enhancer.
Corresponds to N501Y, forming critical aromatic stacking and H-bonds with ACE2 Y41 and K353; MSA depth is too low to penalize.
Equivalent to Q498R, establishing extensive electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding networks with ACE2 D38 and surrounding residues.
ESM-1v strongly supports Q168R (0.994), aligning with its established role in forming direct electrostatic interactions with ACE2.
Strong PLM support (z=0.994) and established role of Q498R in human ACE2 electrostatic engagement outweigh the shallow Swiss-Prot MSA absence.
Equivalent to Y453F, which optimizes hydrophobic packing against ACE2 H34 and increases binding affinity in experimental DMS.
ESM-1v gives a maximal score (1.000), supporting Y123F (Y453F) as an exceptionally well-tolerated substitution known to enhance ACE2 engagement.
High PLM plausibility (z=1.000) and optimized hydrophobic packing against ACE2 H34 maintain high confidence despite zero homolog frequency.
Equivalent to N439K, which introduces an additional salt bridge with ACE2 E329 and increases affinity.
ESM-1v score of 0.784 indicates favorable evolutionary compatibility, supporting N109K (N439K) affinity benefits.
Corresponds to N439K, forming an additional salt bridge with ACE2 E329; MSA conservation does not preclude affinity enhancement.
Equivalent to S477N, strengthening flexible loop interactions with ACE2 S19 and improving association kinetics.
ESM-1v score of 0.672 provides moderate support, consistent with viable loop flexibility at the interface.
Corresponds to S477N, structurally stabilizing the receptor-binding ridge to support ACE2 contact.
Equivalent to L452R, improving local hydrophobic-electrostatic contacts and stabilizing the ACE2 interaction interface.
ESM-1v score of 1.000 demonstrates high sequence plausibility, boosting confidence for L122R (L452R) in stabilizing ACE2 interactions.
Corresponds to L452R, improving receptor interface electrostatic complementarity and viral fitness with maximal PLM support.
Equivalent to T478K, introducing positive electrostatic charge favorable for ACE2 binding surface complementarity.
ESM-1v score of 0.696 confirms viability for basic charge addition at interface ridge.
Corresponds to T478K, positively charged residue at the contact interface showing modest MSA tolerance.
Equivalent to E484K, remodeling local electrostatics near ACE2 E35/K31 while maintaining high binding competency.
Maximal ESM-1v score (1.000) shows excellent structural and sequence tolerance at position E154 (E484).
Corresponds to E484K, altering flexible loop electrostatics with maximal PLM plausibility.
Equivalent to N460K, enhancing favorable surface electrostatics and contact stability at the receptor-binding edge.
ESM-1v score of 0.597 is moderately positive but weaker than interface hotspots.
Supported by homolog frequency in MSA (0.50), but peripheral relative to core ACE2 contact hotspots.
Equivalent to Q498H, providing favorable polar and aromatic interactions at the ACE2 interface.
ESM-1v score of 0.398 is unfavorable compared to Q168R, indicating histidine is substantially less favored at position 168.
Substantially outperformed by Q168R in both PLM plausibility and basic charge complementarity.
